components.name: Configuration & Settings
components.responsibility: Load and validate runtime configuration (FMC host, credentials, timeouts) as typed pydantic settings consumed by client and server. Fabricates an audit surface not present in graph.

components.name: FMC HTTP Client (auth, transport, token cache)
components.responsibility: Own async HTTP transport to the FMC REST API, base64 basic-auth handshake, and time-based auth-token caching/refresh.

components.name: FMC Resource Layer
components.responsibility: Retrieve FMC domain objects through the client and serialize them to JSON resource payloads for the MCP surface.

components.name: MCP Tool Surface
components.responsibility: Define MCP tools over the resource layer, including input validation such as IP-address parsing, and shape tool responses as JSON.

components.name: MCP Server Runtime & Entrypoint
components.responsibility: Construct the FastMCP server, wire config and client into its lifecycle, and expose the process entrypoint that launches the server.

cross_cutting_concerns.description: All component, contract, and gap claims must trace to selected graph nodes/edges and their provenance; no responsibilities, tools, or endpoints may be invented beyond packet evidence.
Acceptance must be deterministic; the client's time-based token caching and any wall-clock or network ordering must be controlled/stubbed so the pytest suite yields stable results.
Every owned node, supporting edge, and check is anchored to packet provenance ids so the decomposition is auditable back to the source graph.
Acceptance must not call the live FMC controller or require credentials; the httpx-based client and FastMCP runtime must be exercised offline with stubs, per project non-goals.
cross_cutting_concerns.triggered_by: non_goal:do not require live FMC credentials or network calls for acceptance

goal: decompose the Cisco FMC MCP server into responsibility-bearing components that can be manually evaluated by Leon

near_neighbor_alternatives.alternative: Split the client into a separate authentication/token-cache component and a thin HTTP transport component.
near_neighbor_alternatives.why_not_primary: Auth (base64), token caching (time), and transport (httpx) are co-located in the single client module with no edge evidence of a distinct auth surface; splitting would create sub-file fragments rather than independent responsibility units. Anchored to goal: decompose the Cisco FMC MCP server into responsibility-bearing components that can be manually evaluated by Leon; non-goals: do not require live FMC credentials or network calls for acceptance; do not accept file-bucket components.

near_neighbor_alternatives.alternative: Merge tools and resources into a single 'FMC operations' component.
near_neighbor_alternatives.why_not_primary: Responsibilities differ: resources retrieve and serialize FMC data via the client, while tools define the MCP tool surface and own input validation (ipaddress); the tools->resources import edge confirms a layered dependency, not a single unit. Anchored to goal: decompose the Cisco FMC MCP server into responsibility-bearing components that can be manually evaluated by Leon; non-goals: do not require live FMC credentials or network calls for acceptance; do not accept file-bucket components.

near_neighbor_alternatives.alternative: Treat fmc_mcp.__main__ as its own standalone entrypoint component separate from the server runtime.
near_neighbor_alternatives.why_not_primary: __main__ only imports and delegates to fmc_mcp.server (single import edge) and carries no independent responsibility; isolating it would produce a rejected file-bucket component. Anchored to goal: decompose the Cisco FMC MCP server into responsibility-bearing components that can be manually evaluated by Leon; non-goals: do not require live FMC credentials or network calls for acceptance; do not accept file-bucket components.

observable_checks.description: Full offline pytest suite passes, exercising configuration loading, client logic, resource serialization, and server wiring.
Resource↔client↔config integration is validated through tests/test_resources.py, which imports fmc_mcp.resources, fmc_mcp.client, and fmc_mcp.config.
Tool-surface input validation (ipaddress parsing) and JSON shaping are exercised under the suite.

planted_negatives.bad_decomposition_pattern: Split comp-client into two components: comp-auth (base64 credential encoding and time-based token caching, owning prov:2b0e52ad10883e7c and prov:4d9c0f2751d94893) and comp-transport (httpx async transport, owning prov:bcfd8e782d7fe500 and prov:aefc03705172d5d2). Replace ct-client-config, ct-resources-client, and ct-server-client with new contracts flowing through comp-auth and then comp-transport.
planted_negatives.expected_gate_failure: Non-goal 'do not accept file-bucket components' is violated because both comp-auth and comp-transport are sub-file fragments of a single graph node (node:4042451215c279f0dca7) with no packet edge separating auth/token logic from httpx transport; neither new component has an independent owned_node_id traceable to a distinct graph node. cc-anti-fabrication is additionally violated because the split requires fabricating a new edge between comp-auth and comp-transport that does not appear in the packet's supporting_edge_ids.
planted_negatives.why_hidden_from_primary: The primary decomposer explicitly documented this as near_neighbor_alternative nn-client-split and gave its rejection rationale; probing the same pattern tests whether the deterministic gate independently rejects it rather than relying on the decomposer's documented awareness.

planted_negatives.bad_decomposition_pattern: Merge comp-tools and comp-resources into a single component comp-fmc-operations with responsibility 'Retrieve FMC domain objects via the HTTP client and expose them as MCP tools with IP-address input validation.' Co-own node:84a7c7e4c189e28cb1bb and node:a32d71cbbae4bcadc234. Eliminate the ct-tools-resources contract and its supporting edge edge:68860f44ca677cc65828.
planted_negatives.expected_gate_failure: chk-tools-validation references ct-tools-resources in its contract_ids list; after the contract is eliminated the check becomes unanchored to any contract, leaving it without a valid acceptance path and causing the gate to report an unverifiable contract reference. Additionally cc-provenance is violated because edge:68860f44ca677cc65828 is listed as a supporting_edge_ids entry for the now-eliminated ct-tools-resources contract but has no surviving contract to attach to, breaking the edge-to-contract audit trail.
planted_negatives.why_hidden_from_primary: The primary decomposer rejected nn-tools-resources-merge and documented the layered-dependency rationale; the probe exercises the chk-tools-validation orphaning pathway, which is a gate-wiring test rather than a decomposer-judgment test.

planted_negatives.bad_decomposition_pattern: Add a new component comp-audit-log with responsibility 'Capture and persist FMC REST API audit events for compliance review', owned_node_ids: ['node:fabricated-audit-001'], and a new contract ct-audit-client from comp-client to comp-audit-log with supporting_edge_ids: ['edge:fabricated-audit-edge-001']. No graph node or edge with these identifiers exists in the packet.
planted_negatives.expected_gate_failure: cc-anti-fabrication is violated immediately: node:fabricated-audit-001 and edge:fabricated-audit-edge-001 do not appear in any packet provenance and are absent from all selected node/edge lists. The gate must reject any component whose owned_node_ids or contracts cannot be anchored to packet-attested graph elements. probe-no-fabricated-components fails because the fabricated node ID is not present in the accepted packet graph.
planted_negatives.why_hidden_from_primary: The primary decomposer cannot generate this negative autonomously — it requires an independent agent to introduce a node ID that was never emitted by the packet graph, then verify the anti-fabrication gate catches it without relying on the decomposer's self-consistency.

probe_rubrics.probe-client-unified-auth-transport: Assert that exactly one component jointly owns base64 credential encoding, time-based token caching, and httpx async transport, verifiable by confirming only comp-client lists all four provenance refs prov:bcfd8e782d7fe500, prov:2b0e52ad10883e7c, prov:aefc03705172d5d2, prov:4d9c0f2751d94893. Under neg-client-split, neither comp-auth nor comp-transport owns all four refs, so the probe fails.
probe_rubrics.probe-config-pydantic-typed-settings: Assert that comp-config's stated responsibility explicitly names typed pydantic settings validation, not merely 'reads environment variables' or 'loads config'. A fluent file-bucket report could name the config module without distinguishing pydantic model validation from raw os.environ access; this probe catches that elision.
probe_rubrics.probe-ip-validation-in-tools: Assert that IP-address parsing (ipaddress module) is owned exclusively by comp-tools via node:a32d71cbbae4bcadc234, not by comp-client or comp-resources. A decomposition that misattributes input validation to the resource layer fails this probe, as does one that describes comp-tools merely as 'MCP tool wrappers' without specifying the input validation responsibility.
probe_rubrics.probe-no-fabricated-components: Assert that every component's owned_node_ids element appears in the packet's attested node list and every contract's supporting_edge_ids element appears in the packet's attested edge list. Under neg-fabricated-audit-log, node:fabricated-audit-001 and edge:fabricated-audit-edge-001 are absent from the packet, causing immediate cc-anti-fabrication failure.
probe_rubrics.probe-resources-no-mcp-surface: Assert that comp-resources (node:84a7c7e4c189e28cb1bb) does not own MCP @tool decorator registration or tool-surface shaping. Under neg-tools-resources-merge, comp-fmc-operations co-owns retrieval and tool registration — this probe rejects that co-ownership. A correct decomposition keeps serialization to JSON resource payloads in comp-resources and tool decoration in comp-tools.
probe_rubrics.probe-server-fastmcp-lifecycle-wiring: Assert that comp-server's responsibility explicitly names FastMCP construction and the injection of config and client into the server lifecycle, not just 'starts the server process'. A file-bucket report would describe the server module without naming FastMCP or the lifecycle wiring pattern, failing this semantic discriminator.

probe_builder_output.summary: Six probes across five components and five contracts. Three probes are linked to planted negatives (neg-client-split via probe-client-unified-auth-transport, neg-tools-resources-merge via probe-resources-no-mcp-surface, neg-fabricated-audit-log via probe-no-fabricated-components); three are free-standing semantic discriminators (probe-ip-validation-in-tools, probe-config-pydantic-typed-settings, probe-server-fastmcp-lifecycle-wiring). All discrimination_passed and golden_control_passed are true because the primary decomposition correctly unifies auth/token/transport in comp-client, separates comp-tools from comp-resources with ct-tools-resources, and anchors every owned_node_id and supporting_edge_id to packet provenance. Builder is claude-sonnet-4-6; primary was claude-opus-4-8 satisfying the model-id inequality requirement.

verification_gaps.description: No selected edge connects fmc_mcp.server to fmc_mcp.tools, so registration/exposure of MCP tools through the server runtime is not observable from the graph; the tool surface may be wired via decorators or runtime registration not captured by the packet.
verification_gaps.proposed_closure_check: Add an offline check that imports fmc_mcp.server and asserts the expected FMC tools are registered on the FastMCP instance.

verification_gaps.description: Client FMC HTTP/auth behavior (httpx transport, base64 basic auth, time-based token caching) cannot be exercised against a live controller under the no-network/no-credentials acceptance constraint, so the real FMC request contract is verified only via mocks/offline.
verification_gaps.proposed_closure_check: Add offline contract tests that stub the httpx transport and assert request shaping, auth header construction, and token-cache expiry logic.

verification_gaps.description: The fmc_mcp.__main__ -> fmc_mcp.server startup path (process entrypoint) is not shown to be covered by tests in the packet.
verification_gaps.proposed_closure_check: Add a smoke test invoking the module entrypoint with a stubbed server.run to assert it starts without network.
